---
title: "Group by Language"
filters:
  - regurgitate
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    group-by-language: true
---

When your document uses multiple programming languages, the appendix can become difficult to navigate. The `group-by-language` option organizes code blocks by language, creating separate sections for Python, R, SQL, and so on.

This is particularly helpful for tutorials that compare implementations across languages, or for polyglot data science workflows.

```yaml
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    group-by-language: true
```

## Data Preparation

We begin by creating our dataset in Python:

```{python}
# Simulated experiment data: treatment vs control
treatment = [23, 25, 28, 24, 26, 27, 29, 25]
control = [19, 21, 20, 22, 18, 20, 21, 19]

print("Treatment group:", treatment)
print("Control group:", control)
```

## Statistical Test

Now we perform the analysis in R, using a built-in t-test:

```{r}
# Two-sample t-test comparing treatment and control
treatment <- c(23, 25, 28, 24, 26, 27, 29, 25)
control <- c(19, 21, 20, 22, 18, 20, 21, 19)

t.test(treatment, control)
```

## Effect Size

Back to Python to compute Cohen's d:

```{python}
# Cohen's d for effect size
import math

def cohens_d(group1, group2):
    n1, n2 = len(group1), len(group2)
    mean1 = sum(group1) / n1
    mean2 = sum(group2) / n2
    
    var1 = sum((x - mean1)**2 for x in group1) / (n1 - 1)
    var2 = sum((x - mean2)**2 for x in group2) / (n2 - 1)
    
    pooled_std = math.sqrt(((n1-1)*var1 + (n2-1)*var2) / (n1+n2-2))
    return (mean1 - mean2) / pooled_std

d = cohens_d(treatment, control)
print(f"Cohen's d = {d:.2f} (large effect)")
```

## Visualization

Finally, a comparison plot in R:

```{r}
# Side-by-side boxplot
boxplot(treatment, control,
        names = c("Treatment", "Control"),
        col = c("coral", "skyblue"),
        main = "Treatment vs Control",
        ylab = "Response")
```
